Alger, 9 novembre 2026 (Algeria Tech) —: Algiers, November 9, 2026 (Algeria Tech) — The past week in cyberspace was marked by three notable events, ranging from the correction of artificial intelligence models by GPT-6 Astra to the postponed release of PostgreSQL 19 in the face of massive bug reports, alongside OpenAI's claimed industrialization of vulnerability research in the Linux kernel.

Des chercheurs du Massachusetts Institut: Researchers from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology report that GPT-6 Astra possesses the ability to interpret the weights of small neural networks, make modifications to them, and design new ones in the absence of any training. By modifying only 0.016% of the weights of the Qwen3.5-0.8B model, Astra boosted its score in mathematics from 7.9% to 48.1%. However, the authors note that this technique remains incapable of integrating a skill initially absent from the model, and the evaluations do not prove Astra's ability to self-improve.

According to Robert Haas, artificial intelligence solutions generate anomaly reports at a rate higher than the review and correction pace of human teams. This backlog has already led to the removal of new features, raising questions about the sustainability of the project's innovation momentum.
Par ailleurs, OpenAI indique que ses age: Meanwhile, OpenAI indicates that its agents exploited 948 flaws within the Linux kernel, giving an unprivileged local user the ability to gain administrator privileges. The automated agent system handles identification, reproduction, and exploitation of the flaws before formulating patches, for a total cost evaluated at $1.2 million. The data indicate a unit cost of $1,280 to uncover and exploit a Linux kernel flaw. These data stem from a prototype, where all exploits and patches require validation by human experts.
